title: fix(core): a registration that declines the bare key no longer clears its stub
body:
Fixes #9839

Clause-②: no — no exported symbol is added, no key on a published payload moves, and no accept set is relaxed. Which registrations the registry ACCEPTS is unchanged; what changes is which bare key survives a registration that declined to take it.

## The defect

`Registry.register`'s bare stub-clearing lines sat OUTSIDE its `meta?.namespace && !meta?.skipFallback` branch. A registration that explicitly DECLINED the bare key therefore skipped the claim and deleted another declaration's bare lazy stub anyway — and the bare key ended up **claimed by nobody at all**: the stub that would have loaded the chunk was gone, and the registration that removed it had refused to replace it. Nothing warned, because from the registry's point of view no one was contesting anything.

### Line numbers, re-taken (the card's were taken before objectui#9838 landed)

Measured on a freshly fetched `origin/main` `6c3944c30` at **2026-09-18T09:59:54Z**. `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts` is byte-identical between that ref and this branch's base `276d17459` (`git diff --quiet` exit 0), so both readings describe the same file.

| what | card said (pre-objectui#9838) | re-taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `if (meta?.namespace && !meta?.skipFallback) {` | `:492` | `:505` |
| `this.components.set(type, {` — the bare-key claim, INSIDE | `:506` | `:547` |
| branch ends | `:511` | `:552` |
| `this.lazyEntries.delete(fullType);` | `:515` | `:556` |
| `this.lazyEntries.delete(type);` — outside, unconditional | `:516` | `:557` |
| `unregister(...)` | `:530` | `:571` |
| the `components` ownership guard inside it | `:534`-`:536` | `:577` |
| the unguarded lazy pair inside it | `:538`-`:539` | `:579` / `:580` |
| docblock saying "plus any matching lazy stub" | `:521`-`:523` | `:561`-`:570`, phrase on `:564` |

## The repair

The bare stub-clearing now sits **inside** that branch, under the same predicate that takes the key — the predicate is shared, not duplicated. `this.lazyEntries.delete(fullType)` stays below and unconditional, which is what keeps a no-namespace registration clearing the bare stub: its full type IS the bare key.

⛔ It does not touch which registrations are accepted. No `components` write moved. Stop condition 1 not reached.

## The `unregister` phrase, ruled

The docblock promised "the bare-name fallback (when the fallback still points at this registration), plus any **matching** lazy stub". Ruled here as **"a stub that belongs to this registration"**, from the code's own behaviour rather than from the wording:

`unregister` already answers that exact question for the bare `components` key, and answers it "ownership" — it will not drop bare `dashboard` while it resolves to `plugin-dashboard:dashboard`. Reading the stub line as unconditional makes the **same call**, on the **same bare key**, with the **same owner**, decide the opposite way purely because the owner happens to be sitting in the other table at that instant — and which table it is sitting in is exactly the "has the chunk loaded yet" race that objectui#9533 and objectui#9821 are about. A policy that flips on chunk-load timing is not a policy.

⭐ It is also not hypothetical: with `register` repaired and `unregister` left alone, the identical victim survives one function down — `unregister('dashboard', 'view')` after a declined registration still takes bare `dashboard` off `plugin-dashboard`. The pin `unregister leaves a bare stub that belongs to a DIFFERENT full type` is that case.

⚠️ The BARE form, `unregister(type)` with no namespace, is deliberately **unchanged** and still unconditional on both tables. That is the force form teardown sites pair with the namespaced call (`html-page-lazy-blocks.test.tsx` calls both), and the `components` half has the same asymmetry. Pinned by `the BARE unregister form stays unconditional on both tables`.

## ⭐ The teaching sweep — triage's escalation clause asks about the SOURCE

Triage asked whether any doc or example teaches `skipFallback: true` as the way to avoid affecting another declaration, because "那句话正在制造受害者". **It does — eight places.** Swept at `origin/main` `6c3944c30`, 2026-09-18T09:59:32Z:

| file | line | the teaching |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md` | 425 | `skipFallback: true,  // Don't overwrite other 'form' registrations` — the literal prescription |
| `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md` | 163 | "**Use `skipFallback: true`** when multiple plugins register the same base type" |
| `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md` | 72 | the key table: "Don't register non-namespaced fallback (prevents overwrites)" |
| `skills/objectui/evals/plugin-development.json` | 25 | the graded expected answer to "my plugin registers 'form' but it conflicts" IS `skipFallback: true` |
| `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts` | 504 | `// Skip this if skipFallback is true to avoid overwriting other components` — sitting on the very branch whose delete ran anyway |
| `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts` | 179-181 | the `skipFallback` JSDoc: "This avoids conflicts with other components that share the same base name" |
| `packages/plugin-grid/README.md` | 68 / `content/docs/plugins/plugin-grid.mdx` 203 | "Bare `grid` is deliberately not ours. `skipFallback: true` ... keeps this plugin from claiming it" |
| `packages/plugin-form/README.md` | 57 / `content/docs/plugins/plugin-form.mdx` 356 | "bare `line_items` is left to whoever else claims it" |

Every one of those promised something the code did not deliver whenever the other declaration's claim was a **pending lazy stub**. ⚠️ **Whether that escalates the grade is triage's call, ⛔ not this PR's and ⛔ not the seat's.** The fix is the same either way, and after it every sentence in that table is true. ⛔ None of those files is edited here — they are outside this card's declared file surface, and they no longer need editing for truth.

## The one existing green test this changed, named

⚠️ Making the delete conditional turned exactly **one** existing test red, and it is the named probe stop condition 2 exempts — measured before any test or string was touched: `skipFallback on the EAGER door does not preserve the stub's bare claim`. Everything else in `packages/core` stayed green (155 files / 3292 tests). It is rewritten to assert the repair and renamed to `skipFallback on the EAGER door preserves the stub's bare claim`.

⚠️ **A second existing test was rewritten, and it did NOT go red on its own** — reporting it by name because that is the interesting case: `each door prescribes the remedy that is true for it`. The code change leaves it green while falsifying its premise. That pin asserts the eager door's collision warning says `skipFallback: true` "does not settle this one, because registering ... clears the bare stub either way" — a reason this change removes. Its own comment says it is "⛔ Not a wording preference: the eager door must not prescribe an opt-out that the test above shows does not settle the contest", and "the test above" is the probe that now shows the opposite. So the warning text is repaired (a false console warning shipped by the PR that falsifies it is the worst option), and that pin inverts with it — both doors now prescribe the opt-out, and it asserts the stale disclaimer is gone.

## Tests, and proof they can fail

Run at repo root per AGENTS.md; heavy runs serialized through `../objectstack/scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/` — **155 files / 3292 tests, exit 0**
- `pnpm test --shard=1/4` — **805 passed, 1 skipped (806 files), exit 0**, 801s
- the 47-file at-risk population — **1557 tests, exit 0**. That set is every test that can observe this change, derived mechanically: a test must create a lazy stub (`registerLazy`), call `.unregister(`, or assert on the collision warning text. `pnpm check:registry-bare-names` independently reports the production blast radius: 425 registration claims, 237 bare keys claimed, 59 declined with `skipFallback`, **1 contested** and already in its ledger.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` exit 0 (after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/core^...' build`; the changed test file is genuinely covered — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` names it)
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core lint` exit 0 — 258 files, 0 errors
- gates: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:registry-bare-names`, `check:doc-types`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:changeset-presence` — all exit 0. `check:sdui-registration-pins` exits **2 = prerequisite not met** (wants a console build); NOT MEASURED locally, left to CI. Shards 2-4 left to CI.

### Ablation — four legs, each mutation proven on disk and each restore proven against HEAD

Run through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which refuses a mutation whose anchor misses and asserts the blob moved; each leg restored with `blob == HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Run from the committed fix, so the restore leg has a real restore point.

| leg | mutation | red, exactly as predicted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | put `lazyEntries.delete(type)` back below the branch (the defect) | `skipFallback on the EAGER door preserves the stub's bare claim` + `unregister leaves a bare stub that belongs to a DIFFERENT full type` |
| 2 | drop `unregister`'s ownership guard | `unregister leaves a bare stub that belongs to a DIFFERENT full type` only — the two bare-form pins stayed green, so the guard is precisely targeted |
| 3 | delete the in-branch clear entirely | `a registration that DOES claim the bare key still clears the stub` + `the ordinary stub-then-real lifecycle still clears BOTH stub keys` |
| 4 | restore the pre-fix warning remedy text | `each door prescribes the remedy that is true for it` |

Leg 3 is the one that matters for the opposite-direction case the card asks for: it proves those assertions are not vacuously true. ⛔ No ablation artefact is left in the tree — `git status` is clean and every restore printed its blob equality.

## Seat note — the fence was amended, and this section replaces a now-false one

⚠️ **Edited by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat** (`session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`), 2026-09-18T10:16Z. The dev writes a PR body once and ⛔ never patches it; the body is the seat's to correct, and this section is the correction. It previously said `.changeset/9821-registerlazy-cross-table-collision-warning.md` was deliberately NOT edited. **That is no longer true**, and leaving it would be the exact defect this round exists to close — a false sentence sitting where people read it.

**What changed and why.** That pending changeset (from objectui#9838, same release) ended by saying the eager door cannot prescribe `skipFallback: true` 「because it clears the bare stub whether or not the fallback is taken」. This PR removes precisely that reason, so the sentence would have published **false** into `@object-ui/core`'s CHANGELOG. ⭐ The dev flagged it and **refused to widen its own surface**, which is correct; the seat then amended the fence by exactly that one file and one sentence. It now puts the old reason in past tense, names objectui#9839 as what removed it, and states what is true: declining the bare key leaves it with its owner, and both doors prescribe the opt-out.

⚠️ **This lane's most repeated defect is a false sentence that publishes — three instances in one shift** (objectui#9710's changeset stated a mechanism measured false; its next round left 「`packages/types` is untouched」 standing while the diff moved 62 lines there; this is the third). ⛔ Not a fourth.

**Gates on the final diff, measured before this note was written.** `check-changeset-presence` exit 0 · `check-changeset-claims` exit 0 · `check-changeset-overwrite` exit **0** in its default **report-only** mode (exit 1 only under `OS_CHANGESET_OVERWRITE_ENFORCE=1`). Its finding names `M .changeset/9821-…` and prints `declared at base: @object-ui/core: patch` / `declares now: @object-ui/core: patch` ⇒ the hazard that gate exists for — a colliding filename silently destroying a third party's release declaration — demonstrably did **not** happen, and its own header names this shape as the legitimate one.

**One residual, recorded rather than hidden.** That paragraph still OPENS with 「The two doors give different advice on purpose.」, which this change also falsifies. ⛔ Left as is, by seat decision: the paragraph's closing clause explicitly names that it supersedes its own opening sentence, so the text carries its correction inline rather than elsewhere, and the opener is not actionable on its own — a reader deciding whether to use `skipFallback` reads on and gets the right answer. ⚠️ Stated as a judgement call with its cost, not as a clean result: a reader who skims only the first line gets the stale impression.

**The three pending changesets `check-changeset-claims` flags for naming `Registry.ts` were read as paragraphs and judged against the final diff**, each with a same-command control: `6067-component-meta-derive-from-canonical` (the key list is byte-identical between base and head), `componentinput-reexport-4972` (no `ComponentInput` line in the diff), `default-children-retired-5051` (`defaultChildren` absent; control `skipFallback` matches 13×). ⛔ None falsified.
